meaning: because (I was busy) doing …, so something else didn't happen
nuance: The first clause is an activity that took up time or attention; the result is usually something missed. Both clauses share the same subject.

contrasts.note: -는 바람에 is a sudden outside event; -느라고 is your own time-consuming activity.

examples.en: I was doing homework, so I couldn't answer the phone.
I was swamped getting ready to move.

cloze.en: I was watching a movie last night, so I didn't get any sleep.

mnemonic: It's the sturdier cousin of -아/어도: 도 is still the 'even' at the end.
meaning: even if; even though (concession, often hypothetical)
nuance: A firmer, more deliberate 'even if' than -아/어도, typically for a hypothetical or for a fact the speaker concedes. The main clause can be almost anything: a statement, a resolution (-겠다), advice, a command, or a suggestion. See also HowtoStudyKorean Lesson 112.

examples.ko: 결과가 기대에 못 미치더라도 끝까지 해 보는 게 중요하다.
examples.en: Even if the results fall short of expectations, what matters is seeing it through.
Even if you're running late, be sure to let me know.

cloze.en: However busy you are, make sure you eat breakfast.

nearMiss.hint: Fine in meaning; the cue asks for -더라도.
